# Adleman and Vanderwees — Lacan’s Psychoanalytic Rhetoric (2021)

## Chicago 18 forms

**Full note:** Daniel Adleman and Chris Vanderwees, “Lacan’s Psychoanalytic Rhetoric and the Power of Non-Understanding,” *English Studies in Canada* 47, nos. 2–3 (2021): 201–27, https://doi.org/10.1353/esc.2021.a919374.

**Shortened note:** Adleman and Vanderwees, “Lacan’s Psychoanalytic Rhetoric,” 221–25.

**Bibliography:** Adleman, Daniel, and Chris Vanderwees. “Lacan’s Psychoanalytic Rhetoric and the Power of Non-Understanding.” *English Studies in Canada* 47, nos. 2–3 (2021): 201–27. https://doi.org/10.1353/esc.2021.a919374.

## Essay use

The article gives a sustained, open-access scholarly reconstruction of the brick-wall sequence, pp. 221–25. It reads the wall as a figure of non-understanding, reverberation, and a limit internal to analytic discourse. Its direct quotations from Price’s *Talking to Brick Walls* are a lawful, typeset secondary witness; the primary quotations remain separately marked `source-matched` in the Lacan source until direct edition collation.

**Claim boundary:** the authors’ account of a “blank screen,” echo, and non-understanding is their secondary reception. It cannot make `S/s = X/x`, establish a Jungian correspondence, or turn Lacanian discourse into a proof of QL.

> “Figuring the unresponsive interlocutor as a brick wall conveys the position of the analyst as a ‘blank screen,’ whose role is to help the analysand hear their own discourse as it echoes from the walls of the consulting room.”
